about.title: Los Gatos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Los Gatos families are still absorbing the weight of the 2 traffic deaths recorded in the most recent reporting year alongside 146 people injured across town. Corridors like SR-17, SR-85, and Blossom Hill Road see steady traffic, particularly on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. when crash reports tend to rise. If a loved one died because of another party's negligence on these roads or elsewhere in town, California law allows certain family members to pursue a civil wrongful death claim, separate from any criminal proceeding. This isn't about reliving the tragedy in a courtroom sense—it's about understanding what financial and emotional losses can be recognized under the law, and whether pursuing that path makes sense for your family. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families in Los Gatos with an independent attorney who can walk through the options at no upfront cost, so you can focus on your family while someone reviews the legal side.

whyChoose.title: What Los Gatos Families Should Know

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing primarily to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An independent attorney can help clarify who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity—say, involving road design on a county-maintained stretch—carry a much shorter window. Waiting to sort out details can quietly cost a family its legal options.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Financial
items.desc: California law recognizes not just funeral costs and lost income, but also the loss of a loved one's companionship, guidance, and support. A knowledgeable attorney can help a family understand how these losses are documented and presented.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim require a criminal case first?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it can proceed whether or not criminal charges are ever filed against the responsible party. Many families pursue a civil claim even when no criminal case exists at all.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Los Gatos?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity is involved—for instance, a claim tied to road conditions on a county road like Blossom Hill Road—the deadline to act is much shorter, so it's worth getting guidance early.

items.question: What if more than one family member wants to bring a claim?
items.answer: California law identifies who has standing, typically starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to other dependents in some cases. An independent attorney can help sort out who is eligible to bring the claim and how any recovery might be shared among family members.
